subject: general
question: A shopkeeper purchased an item listed at ₹1,600 after receiving two successive discounts of 35% and 5% from the wholesaler. The shopkeeper then changed the list price so as to gain 25% after allowing 5% discount. For how much did he list the item?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) = 1600 × (65/100) × (95/100) = ₹988

Required Selling Price (SP) to gain 25% = 988 × (125/100) = ₹1235

New List Price (MP) after 5% discount = 1235 × (100/95) = ₹1300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original List Price = ₹1,600

Successive discounts from wholesaler = 35% and 5%

Desired profit for shopkeeper = 25%

Discount allowed on new list price = 5%

 
 Old MP = ₹1600
 
 

 

 -35% & -5%
 Discounts
 
 
 CP = ₹988
 
 
 SP = ₹1235
 
 
 MP = ₹1300
 
 

 

 +25% Profit
 
 

 

 -5% Discount
 
 New List Price = ₹1300

**Calculations:**

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = Original List Price × (1 − 35/100) × (1 − 5/100)

⇒ CP = 1600 × 0.65 × 0.95 = ₹988

⇒ Selling Price (SP) for a 25% profit = CP × (1 + 25/100)

⇒ SP = 988 × 1.25 = ₹1235

⇒ The new Marked Price (MP) must allow a 5% discount to arrive at the SP.

⇒ SP = MP × (1 − 5/100)

⇒ 1235 = MP × 0.95

⇒ MP = 1235 ÷ 0.95 = ₹1300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two discounts a% and b% are given successively, the equivalent single discount can be calculated directly using the formula: (a + b − ab/100)%.

Marked Price & Cost Price Relation

The direct ratio between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP) can be given by: CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

Effective Multiplier Concept

For repeated percentage changes, the final value is found by multiplying the base value by scaling factors: Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± x/100) × (1 ± y/100).
